properties.entry: Whether the user can resize the columns by dragging the right edge of a header. The table has a ResizableColumnsBehavior then and grows as a column does; the selection, #, Actions and ID columns cannot be resized.
Whether the table is as wide as its columns or takes the full width of the page, following the size of the window until a column is resized.
Whether the columns share the width by their content or by proportions the page sets.
Where the paging links, the rows per page and the actions on the whole table are shown: above the headers, below the rows or both.
Where the bar offering to select every user is shown, once every row of the page is selected.

The unit of the height of the body. Choosing one sets the height to 800 pixels, or to 100 percent of the parent's or the window's height. Percent of the parent gives the table a parent 600 pixels high.
The height of the rows between the headers and the footer, in the unit above. Only the rows scroll; a negative height lets the body take the height of its rows.
Where the edit form and the delete confirmation are shown: over the table only, or over the whole page.
Which icons the actions show: the ones built into ui-components, the Font Awesome icons as inline SVG, or the same icons drawn by the Font Awesome font.
Where the order, visibility and widths of the columns are kept: in the session, or in a file of the temporary directory that survives restarts of the server.

Where the browser fetches the rows from: an Ajax behavior of the table on this page, or the resource mounted at /api/users, a stateless request that does not touch the page, with the page, the sort and the filter in its URL. Paging, sorting and selecting go through the page either way.

Whether the table shows its users a page at a time, or in one list that grows by the next 25 users whenever the body is scrolled to its end. The paging links and the rows per page are left out then, and the veil blocks the table while the users load.
How many users can be selected: none hides the selection column, one keeps a single row selected, many selects any number of rows and offers to select all of them.

Whether the navigation tells how many users are selected, such as "2 selected", next to its actions, with a waste bin that deselects them all: a SelectionCountToolbarAction added to the table, turned on and off here.

Whether going to another page or choosing another number of rows per page deselects every user (setClearSelectionOnNavigation of the table), or the selection is kept while paging. Sorting deselects every user either way.
